high.title: Analysis: Brasília Pressures, Interest Rates React and the Market Loses Conviction
high.summary: Brazil ended the week with the Ibovespa hovering around 175,000 points, pressured by a challenging international environment and deteriorating domestic fiscal expectations amid an increasingly complex electoral scenario. The IBC-Br (economic activity index) for March contracted 0.7% month-on-month, in line with market expectations, serving as a GDP preview. Despite weaker economic data suggesting activity moderation, this appears insufficient to significantly relieve pressure on the Central Bank. The prevailing market view is that the monetary authority seeks to preserve space to continue the interest rate cutting cycle, but the combination of persistent inflation, adverse external conditions, and deteriorating fiscal expectations increases the probability of a pause in the cutting cycle. This creates a challenging environment for BRL and Brazilian assets, as fiscal concerns continue to undermine market confidence while the BCB faces limited room for dovish monetary policy.

medium.title: US Interest Rates: Watching Inflation and Iran War, Market Already Prices Rate Hike in October
medium.summary: Recent Middle East peace negotiation impasse and oil prices above $100 have led markets to advance bets on US rate hikes to October 2026. The CME FedWatch tool shows 51.7% probability of Fed rate increases in October, with traders seeing 39.9% chance of 25bp hike. This shift in US monetary policy expectations creates headwinds for Brazilian assets and BRL, as higher US rates typically drive capital flows away from emerging markets.

medium.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Falls to $74,000 with Nearly $1 Billion in Liquidations; See Cryptocurrency Prices This Saturday (23)
medium.summary: Bitcoin traded around $74,000 with nearly 3% decline as global crypto markets fell with $940 million in liquidations over 24 hours. While not directly impacting traditional Brazilian markets, crypto volatility can influence risk sentiment and capital flows, particularly as Brazilian investors increasingly participate in digital asset markets.
